The core insight lies in modeling ball dynamics as a constrained optimization problem over a factor graph. Each node represents a potential ball location/state, connected by edges encoding valid transitions based on physical laws and player behavior. The formulation enforces that at any given time, only one ball state and position are active, ensuring temporal coherence. Constraints include kinematic bounds (zero acceleration during free flight, bounded deceleration during roll), and logical dependencies derived from player interaction. This dual enforcement—physical realism and interaction fidelity—addresses key failure modes like motion blur and occlusion. The mixed-integer program allows for discrete decisions regarding ball ownership and state changes, which are essential for accurate tracking in complex scenes.
